reason: The current GraphRecommender achieves host validation macro HR@10 of 0.6225, but its history-attention query depends only on the propagated user vector, limiting adaptation to the latest interaction. Historical successes support testing explicit sequential context, while failed objective and embedding changes favor preserving the current backbone and training objective. Modify model_design for the focused query extension and training_evaluation for diagnostics and faithful checkpoint restoration; Electronics' lower HR@10 motivates the hypothesis but does not establish its cause.

plan.model_design: Add self.history_last = nn.Linear(dim, dim, bias=False) to GraphRecommender and initialize its weight to zero, implementing the architectural change q = self.history_query(u) + self.history_last(v_last). In encode_history, use the existing validity mask to gather the rightmost valid item's propagated vector from item_vectors, explicitly replacing it with zero for fully masked histories; do not assume the final tensor position contains an item because histories are right padded. Apply the combined query before the existing unsqueeze and additive attention, retaining keys, relative-position embeddings, values, attention normalization, fusion gate and candidate scoring unchanged. This tests latest-interaction context within the existing network, drawing on historical sequential-context successes without introducing their Transformer blocks, distance biases, objective changes or separate embedding tables. Preserve GraphRecommender.__init__, encode_history, forward, predict_indices, predict_history and all existing attribute names and dimensions; isolate initialization of the zeroed projection from the training RNG so existing parameter initialization remains reproducible.
plan.training_evaluation: Update write_predictor so working/predict.py reconstructs the modified GraphRecommender and strictly restores history_last.weight with the full state dictionary from exactly one newly trained, selected checkpoint per category, preserving all four dataset routes and existing function signatures. Extend check_history_fusion within its existing RNG-forked diagnostic scope to verify zero-initialization parity with the original query, rightmost-valid-item extraction for repeated, singleton and padded histories, unchanged empty-history behavior, finite projection gradients, and checkpoint reload prediction parity; use a temporary nonzero projection to check query sensitivity and restore it before fitting. Keep graph construction, supervised-edge masking, prefix sampling, negative sampling, history length, dimensions, propagation depth, loss, optimizer, regularization, gate, batching, steps, checkpoint selection, early stopping and category time limits unchanged, with SASREC_EPOCHS defaulting to 200. Preserve preprocessing seed 0 through unchanged supplied splits, training and evaluation seed 42, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], single-GPU execution, trial-local artifacts and identical local-validation/predictor history processing, without accessing hidden tests, other trials or external data. Reload each selected checkpoint to print its actual local macro HR@10 as Final Validation Score, and use the pinned host protocol of 200 validation users per category and 99 unique negatives to assess improvement over 0.6225; treat the proposed 0.005–0.015 gain as an unmeasured hypothesis and never average checkpoints or combine independently fitted scorers.
